notes: The ASV note *The Hebrew text has taken, taken* corroborates the doubled אָחֻז; the first occurrence is the rendered one and the second is unrepresented under rule 22.

*who was* is taken as one added frame because the Hebrew writes an appositional מִן־הַלֵּוִי and no clause at all, so both supplied words compose the single office of making that phrase a relative clause (rule 2's `טוֹב־עַיִן הוּא` reasoning). The competing reading gives *was* to the מִן as rule 49's copula and marks only *who* added; it is named in the unit's note.
לִפְנֵי is split rather than fused here, the ASV spending *in* on the preposition and *the presence* on the construct noun, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is unmet.
